questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the king of Judah, his servants, and his people to do?
questions.a: They are to listen to the word of Yahweh, act justly, and rescue those who have been robbed by their oppressors. They are not to mistreat foreigners, orphans, or widows, and they are not to harm anyone or kill innocent people.

questions.q: What will happen if the king obeys these commands?
questions.a: Kings from David’s line will continue to enter the gates of the palace, riding in chariots and on horses, with their officials and people.

questions.q: What happens if they do not listen to these words of Yahweh’s declaration?
questions.a: The royal palace will become a ruin.

questions.q: How will the palace become a wilderness?
questions.a: Yahweh will send destroyers who will cut down its choicest cedars and throw them into the fire.

questions.q: Why has Yahweh done these things to the great city?
questions.a: He has done them because the people abandoned the covenant and worshiped other gods.

questions.q: Why should the people weep for the one who is going away?
questions.a: They should weep for him because he will never return or see his native land again.

questions.q: What will happen to Shallum?
questions.a: Shallum will die in the place where his enemies exiled him, and he will never see his land again.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say the king does to those who build his house?
questions.a: He makes them work for nothing and does not pay their wages, even though he builds himself a great house with spacious rooms, cedar paneling, and red paint.

questions.q: What should a good king do?
questions.a: He should do justice even for the poor and needy, do righteousness, and know Yahweh.

questions.q: Why will the people not lament for king Jehoiakim when he dies?
questions.a: They will not lament for him because he steals, kills innocent people, and oppresses others.

questions.q: What kind of burial will they give Jehoiakim?
questions.a: They will bury him the way people bury a donkey, dragging his body and throwing it out beyond the gates of Jerusalem.

questions.q: Where should the people of Jerusalem cry out?
questions.a: They should cry out from Lebanon, Bashan, and Abarim because their allies have been destroyed.

questions.q: What has been the custom of the people since they were young?
questions.a: They have not listened to Yahweh’s voice.

questions.q: What will happen to them when they do not listen?
questions.a: They will lose their leaders, their allies will become captives, and they will be ashamed and despised.

questions.q: What will happen to the people who live like a bird nesting in the cedars of Lebanon?
questions.a: People will pity them, and they will suffer greatly, like a woman giving birth.

questions.q: What will happen to Coniah?
questions.a: Yahweh will give Coniah into the hand of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and send him and his mother to another land, where he will die.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about the land Coniah and his mother long to return to?
questions.a: They desire to return to it, but they will never go back there.

questions.q: What do people compare Coniah to?
questions.a: They compare him to a broken pot that no one wants, because enemy soldiers will force him and his children into a foreign land they do not know.

questions.q: What does Yahweh command the land to do?
questions.a: He commands the land to listen to the word of Yahweh.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about Coniah?
questions.a: Yahweh says Coniah will be left childless and will not succeed, because no descendant of his will rule as king over Judah.

commentary.text: Justice is recommended, and destruction threatened in case of disobedience. (Jer. 22:1-9) The captivity of Jehoiakim, and the end of Jeconiah. (Jer. 22:10-19) The doom of the royal family. (Jer. 22:20-30)

Jer. 22:1-9 The king of Judah is spoken to, as sitting upon the throne of David, the man after God's own heart. Let him follow his example, that he may have the benefit of the promises made to him. The way to preserve a government, is to do the duty of it. But sin will be the ruin of the houses of princes, as well as of meaner men. And who can contend with destroyers of God's preparing? God destroys neither persons, cities, nor nations, except for sin; even in this world he often makes it plain for what crimes he sends punishment; and it will be clear at the day of judgement.

Jer. 22:10-19 Here is a sentence of death upon two kings, the wicked sons of a very pious father. Josiah was prevented from seeing the evil to come in this world, and removed to see the good to come in the other world; therefore, weep not for him, but for his son Shallum, who is likely to live and die a wretched captive. Dying saints may be justly envied, while living sinners are justly pitied. Here also is the doom of Jehoiakim. No doubt it is lawful for princes and great men to build, beautify, and furnish houses; but those who enlarge their houses, and make them sumptuous, need carefully to watch against the workings of vain-glory. He built his houses by unrighteousness, with money gotten unjustly. And he defrauded his workmen of their wages. God notices the wrong done by the greatest to poor servants and labourers, and will repay those in justice, who will not, in justice, pay those whom they employ. The greatest of men must look upon the meanest as their neighbours, and be just to them accordingly. Jehoiakim was unjust, and made no conscience of shedding innocent blood. Covetousness, which is the root of all evil, was at the bottom of all. The children who despise their parents' old fashions, commonly come short of their real excellences. Jehoiakim knew that his father found the way of duty to be the way of comfort, yet he would not tread in his steps. He shall die unlamented, hateful for oppression and cruelty.

Jer. 22:20-30 The Jewish state is described under a threefold character. Very haughty in a day of peace and safety. Very fearful on alarm of trouble. Very much cast down under pressure of trouble. Many never are ashamed of their sins till brought by them to the last extremity. The king shall close his days in bondage. Those that think themselves as signets on God's right hand, must not be secure, but fear lest they should be plucked thence. The Jewish king and his family shall be carried to Babylon. We know where we were born, but where we shall die we know not; it is enough that our God knows. Let it be our care that we die in Christ, then it will be well with us wherever we die, thought it may be in a far country. The Jewish king shall be despised. Time was when he was delighted in; but all those in whom God has no pleasure, some time or other, will be so lowered, that men will have no pleasure in them. Whoever are childless, it is the Lord that writes them so; and those who take no care to do good in their days, cannot expect to prosper. How little is earthly grandeur to be depended upon, or flourishing families to be rejoiced in! But those who hear the voice of Christ, and follow him, have eternal life, and shall never perish, neither shall any enemy pluck them out of his almighty hands.
